title: Your AI agent should not have permission to do what it recommends.
hook: Your AI agent should not have permission to do what it recommends.
thesis: The technical position: recommendation and authorization are different capabilities owned by different machinery. The model recommends; a deterministic capability path (principal, target, account control, capability grant, policy, budget, duplicate, pending, state, provider support) decides whether execution is allowed; the adapter executes; independent observation verifies. The hook is earned by showing that exact decision path and naming the boundary where a recommendation can never become a permission on its own.

proven: The directive defines the proposal-to-authorization pipeline and the reason it exists (sections 9, 35).
partial: The live capability decision path matches the named checks.
unknown: A public walkthrough of one real proposal being denied or gated at a specific check.

approval_gate: Nolan approves every exact post. Silence is not approval.
